task: t50 data-side independent profile of table_9 / table_extra_9 (NATIONAL_TEAM_CONTAINER)

evidence_level.L1: payload decode, frame selection, row/block framing, closure, histograms, probes recomputed here
evidence_level.L2: client vs server identity/ordinal agreement and t9 vs t10 row-id agreement (all data-side)

footer_fields_observed.note: the trailing 8 bytes are what close the tiling; the last row's marker byte is also the first byte of a 9-byte reading, so 8-vs-9 footer split is not separable from data (9-byte reading leaves no valid tiling: footer=9 -> 0 walks)

identity_census.identity_structure: ordinal | row_id | row_id | 0x00 (13 bytes at row end)
identity_census.note: row_id 0 is never the chosen tail value; it appears only as a decoy match inside row bodies, which is why accepting zero ids explodes the walk count in the sensitivity table

framing_sensitivity.reading: footer=8 is the unique split that closes; header 11..15 all close identically because no identity lands in the 11..15 window, so the header/selector split is NOT decided by data; zero-id acceptance and monotonicity are what turn a unique closure into an ambiguous one.

closure.block_internal_grammar: unknown; only the ordinal+name marker prefix is located
closure.footer_note: no footer separates from the last block on this member, unlike table_9 where 8 trailing bytes close the tiling; the last block runs to payload end

ambiguity.note: ambiguity is inside the block, not in the block start: every block start is forced

identity_predicate_trial.what: the t9 13-byte identity predicate is applied to this member unchanged
identity_predicate_trial.verdict: NEGATIVE: every variant dies at row 1, so the t9 identity tail does not exist on this member

identity_structure_counterexample.why: the ordinal is a block-leading u32 followed by a u32 name length; there is no ordinal|id|id|00 tail at the block end, so the t9 identity predicate does not apply
identity_structure_counterexample.note: the mimic count is not evidence of an identity tail: those bytes are block content that happens to repeat a u32; the walk that uses them as boundaries is not closed
